newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MANDELA STUDYING EVENTS IN SIERRA LEONE.
newsitem.headline: MANDELA STUDYING EVENTS IN SIERRA LEONE.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela declined on Tuesday to comment on the coup in Sierra Leone, saying he would wait for a full report on the events before forming an opinion.
Speaking to reporters after a meeting with President Yoweri Museveni of Uganda in Cape Town he said:
"Before we make any firm statement, it is necessary to get a report and not just to act on the basis of what we have seen in the media."
A foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday South Africa would not intervene unless asked to do so by Sierra Leone, where Major Johnny Paul Koromah has appointed himself the new head of state.
"We didn't initiate contact in Zaire either. We have had no such request from Sierra Leone. Let's see what happens if we get it," the spokesman said.
